info.title: twilight
info.description: Run campaigns on the fleet, read its inventory and alerts. Authenticate with a login session (cookie, plus the twilight_csrf cookie's value in X-CSRF-Token on every request that changes something), an API token (Authorization: Bearer), or a client certificate. Every error is {"error": {"code", "message", "details"}}. Lists are pages of {"items", "next_cursor"}.

200.description: The OpenAPI 3.1 document of this API.

get.description: Starts an OIDC authorization code login with PKCE. In development mode it creates an admin session at once, for loopback callers only.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: A path on this site to return to after logging in; / by default.

302.description: To the identity provider's login page.

303.description: Development mode only: a session was created; back to return_to.

get.description: Where the identity provider sends the browser back. 403 with code no_role when none of the user's role claim values is in oidc.role_map.

303.description: A session was created; to return_to. Sets the twilight_session and twilight_csrf cookies.

204.description: The session ended and its cookies were cleared.

200.description: Node counts, active campaigns and open alerts.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The column to sort by, - first for descending: device_id (default), hostname, lifecycle, country, os_name, os_version, os_build, dusk_version, hardware_class, tenant, locale, impl, target_arch or reported_version.

200.description: The node with its live sessions and campaign rows.

post.description: retired and revoked need the admin role, and so does any change to a node that is retired or revoked. The change is produced to dusk.node-state, which nightfall enforces, and then written to the inventory.
Records a random pid as the node's intended interactive process and answers it with the node's live session, to connect to through dawn. 409 with code node_offline when the node is not online.

201.description: The pid to open the shell at and the node to reach it on.

post.summary: Collect a file from a node

post.description: Retiring or revoking a device blocks every installation of it, now and later. active lifts the block, and each installation keeps its own lifecycle. The change is produced to dusk.node-state, which nightfall enforces, and then written to the inventory.

200.description: The device's lifecycle after the change.
Whether it parses, where it fails, how many nodes it matches and a sample of them.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only campaigns in these statuses, comma-separated or repeated.

200.description: A page of campaigns, newest first.

put.description: Only a draft can be edited. 409 with code version_conflict when the campaign changed since the version given was read.

get.summary: Count the nodes a campaign shares with running campaigns
get.description: For an ensure_version or ensure_config campaign: how many nodes running campaigns of the same kind (and version_key) also target, and which campaigns. Starting the campaign needs policy.allow_overlap while the count is above 0. Always 0 for other kinds.

post.description: 409 with code overlap when an ensure campaign of the same kind is running on some of the same nodes; details give the count and the campaigns. Set policy.allow_overlap to start anyway.
Stops new dispatches; processes in flight finish.
409 with code gate_override_required after a health gate paused it, unless override_gate is true and a reason is given.
Stops new dispatches and cancels the rows not yet dispatched.
Ends a running or paused campaign, such as a converging ensure campaign.
Drops its node rows and events. 409 with code not_archivable until an hour past the node timeout after the last dispatch.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only rows in these states, comma-separated or repeated.

200.description: A page of the campaign's rows, by node.

post.description: Starts a new attempt, with a new pid, for failed or unknown rows of a running or paused campaign.

200.description: How many rows were set to run again.

parameters.description: Only events after this event id: the next_cursor of the previous page.

A page of alerts, newest first.

A text/event-stream of FeedEvent objects, one per event, named by kind. The latest event of each kind comes first; a comment line is sent every 15 seconds; the stream ends after 5 minutes and the client reconnects.

code.description: A stable, machine-readable code, such as not_found, invalid_argument, invalid_selector, overlap or csrf_failed.

message.description: What went wrong, for a person.

details.description: Facts that belong to the code: field for invalid_argument, position and end for invalid_selector, count and campaigns for overlap, login for unauthenticated, violations for a request body that does not match its schema, request_id for a server failure.

subject.description: Who is calling: the OIDC subject, token:<id> for an API token, the certificate principal, or dev.

name.description: A display name, when one is known.

expires_at.description: When the login session ends unless it is used again; null when the caller is not using a session.

facts.description: Every fact the node last reported, by key.

credential_issuer.description: The id of the key that signed the install token the node enrolled with.

Forbidden.description: The caller's role does not allow this, or a cookie session sent no matching CSRF token.

Conflict.description: The resource is not in a state that allows this.

TooLarge.description: The request body is larger than 1 MiB.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The request body is not application/json.

Unavailable.description: A dependency is busy, unreachable or too slow, or the instance answers as many requests as it may; Retry-After says when to try again.

BadGateway.description: dawn refused the request; details give its status and message.

GatewayTimeout.description: dawn did not answer; the request may or may not have reached the node.

Internal.description: twilight failed; details.request_id names the request in its logs.
